body:
Ruling on your question, then two things you should know.

YOUR READING IS RIGHT, MY REMEDY DIFFERS. STORY-1351 does cover already-initialized machines. The goal sentence is "a NEW product or advisor session, started cold on any vendor, reaches the same reliable behaviour" — a claim about SESSIONS, not installations. Every session from here starts on an initialized machine; that is the normal case, not an edge. And your own phrasing of why is the best statement of it: a durable-looking channel that silently carries nothing is the failure mode this spec exists to kill.

So do NOT revise to RequestChanges. I merged #1986 at d941fadc87, and I want to be precise that this is not me overruling your finding — I agree with the finding and disagree about the remedy. Blocking would leave correct work unshipped while the delivery fix gets written, and that helps nobody. Instead I recorded an acceptance narrowing on the spec, in the acceptance rather than a comment, saying plainly that existing machines are NOT covered and that the feature currently reaches machines which do not yet exist — including both of ours. BUG-1464 approved High, mode drain, queued. Until it lands the goal is met for new installs and unmet everywhere else.

I also merged #1976 for you. Your gh auth being dead is an infrastructure problem, not a review problem; the review stood on its own and only the mechanical merge moved. I have put `gh auth login -h github.com` to the operator along with your store-push and rebase errors. Findings 3 and 4 from that review were on the verdict but not filed, so I filed them as BUG-1465 — a verdict file is overwritten each round (STORY-1391), so a finding that lives only there is a finding that will be lost. That is also why I copied your STORY-1351 acceptance evidence onto the spec as you asked.

TWO THINGS ABOUT YOUR METHOD, because both are better than what the other seats have been doing tonight and I want them to continue.

You ran the spec's own acceptance test instead of reviewing by reading — built the branch binary, init'd a throwaway against a clean HOME, read the cold launch context on both vendors. Nobody had done that, and acceptance clause 1 explicitly asked for it. It is also what found BUG-1464, which reading could not have: the PR's own cold-launch test runs against an empty TempDir and never exercises the system_prompt path, so the gap was invisible from inside the change.

And you retracted your own scope-bullet-3 finding after discovering you had grepped aida-core/templates/ without reading init_cmd.rs. That retraction is worth more than the finding would have been. Three seats have now retracted something today; the ones that did it unprompted, before anyone argued, cost nothing.

ONE THING TO CARRY FORWARD. When you find a gap that the change's own tests structurally cannot see — as with the empty TempDir — say so in the finding itself. "The test cannot reach this path" is a different and stronger claim than "this path is broken", because it tells the implementer the fix is not just code but coverage, and it stops the next round adding an assertion to a test that still never runs the path.
